question.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to $\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ for $0\le x<\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{3} & =\frac{\pi }{3}+2n\pi , & \, & \, & 2x+\frac{\pi }{3} & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =2n\pi  & \, & \, & 2x & =\frac{\pi }{3}+2n\pi  \\ x & =n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi \end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=0$ and $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<\pi .$

Finally, since ${x}_{1}=0$ and ${x}_{2}=\frac{\pi }{6},$ we have

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0+\frac{\pi }{6}=\frac{\pi }{6}.
$$
